answer: It is necessary to evaluate both group and individual fairness in recommender systems (RSs) to ensure that no groups or individuals are disadvantaged. Group fairness concerns the difference in utility between subject groups, while individual fairness focuses on the variation of utility across all users or items. If only one type of fairness is used, it may lead to a limited understanding of fairness, as metrics for one granularity level cannot be used as a proxy for the other. For instance, group fairness metrics cannot estimate individual fairness, which could result in overlooking unfairness experienced by specific individuals within a group. Therefore, considering both types of fairness provides a more comprehensive view of the fairness of the system.
